{{Quote|A bounty of course. Tel Trevura.''"<br />"''Tel Trevura is dead.''"<br />"''Perhaps not.|Balancesheet and Boba Fett discussing Tel Trevura|<ref name="Warfare" />}}
'''Tel Trevura''' was a criminal who once stole a [[Tel Trevura's JumpMaster 5000|JumpMaster 5000]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Svivren/Legends|Svivren]]. By [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], he had a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on his head but was believed to be [[Death/Legends|dead]]. [[Balancesheet]], an [[Assembler]] [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]], shared information on Trevura to the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|What's the trade?''"<br />"''The datacard, plus fifty percent of the bounty on Trevura. For answers to some questions about D'harhan.''"<br />"''Thirty percent.''"<br />"''Forty.|Fett and Balancesheet bargaining over information about Tel Trevura|<ref name="Warfare" />}}
[[File:Kudar_Mubat.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Kud'ar Mub'at (pictured) concealed information about Tel Trevura's ship crashing in Wild Space.]]
Tel Trevura was a criminal<ref name="Warfare" /> who, by [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">According to ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', [[Kud'ar Mub'at]] was aware of Tel Trevura's [[Thief/Legends|theft]] and subsequent crash of a [[Tel Trevura's JumpMaster 5000|JumpMaster 5000]] before Mub'at's [[Death/Legends|death]], which was depicted during the events of ''[[Hard Merchandise]]''. As ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''Hard Merchandise'' to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the crash must have occurred by that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> had [[Thief/Legends|stolen]] a [[Tel Trevura's JumpMaster 5000|JumpMaster 5000]] [[Starship/Legends|starship]] at [[Blaster/Legends|blasterpoint]] from<ref name="Warfare" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Geonosis Worlds">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> [[Svivren/Legends|Svivren]].<ref name="Warfare" /> Trevura and his stolen Jumpmaster 5000 were involved in a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|skirmish]] that included an [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] and a [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]] above a dark celestial body. During the skirmish, the [[Engine/Legends|engines]] of the A-wing exploded, causing it to be knocked out of the fight.<ref name="FFGXW">{{FFGXW|set=Punishing One Expansion Pack|cardname=Tel Trevura}}</ref> Sometime later, Trevura's [[JumpMaster 5000/Legends|JumpMaster 5000]] crashed onto a [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] [[Unidentified planetoid (Wild Space)|planetoid]]. [[Scout/Legends|Scouts]] discovered and registered the crash but [[Kud'ar Mub'at]], an [[Assembler]] [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]], altered the crash registry to remove Trevura's connection to the ship some point before Mub'at's [[Death/Legends|death]]<ref name="Warfare" /> in 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|ABY]].<ref name="TERC" />

By [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], Trevura was presumed dead; however, there was still an open [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] for him. The information broker [[Balancesheet]], Mub'at's successor and fellow Assembler, had learned of Mub'at's actions with the registry as well as the fact that Trevura was in fact alive. That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Balancesheet revealed Trevura's status as well as Mub'at's alteration of the crash records to the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] as part of an information exchange. The deal included information on Trevura and the [[Niordi]] [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[D'harhan]], as well as Fett agreeing to give Balancesheet forty percent of Trevura's bounty.<ref name="Warfare" />

==Skills and abilities==
Tel Trevura was a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and was known as an escape artist.<ref name="FFGXW2">{{FFGXW2|set=Scum and Villainy Conversion Kit|cardname=Tel Trevura}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Tel Trevura was first mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', which was written by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]].<ref name="Warfare" />
